boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Kock's Plantation record (July 12-13, 1863) in Taylor's Operations in West Louisiana [June-September 1863]. The live campaign label reads Taylor's Operations in Louisiana West of Mississip[pi]. The Union landing at Donaldsonville on July 10-11 is context. Campaign-wide movements (Major's raid, the capture of Brashear City and Bayou Boeuf, the river batteries of July 3-10, the withdrawal to the Teche and the September operations) and multi-action totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Weitzel's and Grover's Divisions, XIX Army Corps [US] and two understrength Confederate brigades [CS]; the live field reads zero. Green says Major's brigade had not over 800 effectives and his own three regiments not over 750, against at least ten transports of troops; prisoners named Weitzel's and Dwight's brigades and part of Grover's command. Irwin says Grover held both banks with two divisions, that Dudley's and Morgan's brigades advanced with Paine in support, and that Green posted four regiments with four guns and three regiments with two guns.
claims.rationale: Green's effective figures and Irwin's unit identifications; the Union advance was two brigades of two divisions present. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Irwin says Morgan, under Birge temporarily commanding Grover's division, handled his brigade badly and exposed Dudley's flank, that Grover rode out and drew in the force, and that Morgan's court-martial conviction was set aside by Banks. Green directed the attack and gave Lane, commanding Major's brigade, his instructions. The frozen commanders are Brigadier Generals Tom Green, Godfrey Weitzel and Cuvier Grover; the live page lists Weitzel and Green. No inspected passage describes Weitzel directing the action.
claims.rationale: Command roles from a history and an interested report; the listed commanders do not receive automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 463 total (US 430; CS 33); the live field reads 498 total (US 465; CS 33). Irwin gives Grover's loss as 2 officers and 54 men killed, officers printed '/' in OCR and 210 men wounded and 3 officers and 183 men captured or missing, 465 in all. Green says his loss did not exceed 3 killed and 30 wounded and puts the enemy's at little less than 1,000, over 500 killed and wounded with about 250 prisoners.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Irwin's 465 matches the live Union figure, not the frozen 430.

open_questions: Grover's No. 8 and Dudley's No. 9 reports, Faries's No. 13 and Taylor's No. 10 reports, the Union returns and the Morgan court-martial record remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Richard B. Irwin's History of the Nineteenth Army Corps (Putnam's, 1892), already registered for the Red River pass, is an interested Union history by the corps' assistant adjutant-general. Its chapters cite and quote Stickney's and Green's reports, so it is not independent of them. Green's June 27 dispatch and July 3, July 14 and October 2, 1863 reports, with his undated casualty statement (Official Records Series I, Volume XXVI, Part 1, a shared container), are one interested Confederate family; Taylor's printed indorsements are not part of it. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
